Answer: D
Reason: The imaging sequence demonstrates a rapid progression from initial interstitial opacities to severe bilateral alveolar consolidations, followed by complete radiological resolution in the follow-up films (Figures 5a and 5b). This pattern of fulminant pulmonary involvement with total clearance is characteristic of Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis), distinguishing it from conditions like Goodpasture syndrome or crack lung which typically leave residual fibrosis or have different clinical courses.
